items.stem:
DOCUMENT-BASED QUESTION

Directions: The following question is based on the three documents below. Analyze each document using the HIPP framework (Historical context, Intended audience, Purpose, Point of view). Then construct a well-organized argument in response to the prompt.

PROMPT: Using all three documents and your knowledge of the Gilded Age, evaluate the following claim: "The rapid industrialization of the United States between 1877 and 1900 created prosperity for some Americans while systematically exploiting others, and the mechanisms workers and government used to respond were fundamentally inadequate to address the structural inequality industrialization produced."

Construct an argument that agrees, disagrees, or qualifies this claim using evidence from all three documents and at least two additional pieces of outside historical knowledge. Your response should address the perspectives of at least two groups — industrial workers, industrialists, or policymakers — and evaluate the effectiveness of their strategies.

─────────────────────────────────────────
DOCUMENT 1
Source: Andrew Carnegie, "The Gospel of Wealth," North American Review, June 1889. Available through the Library of Congress digital collections.

"The man who dies thus rich dies disgraced. Such, in my opinion, is the true Gospel concerning Wealth, obedient to which is the duty of the man of Wealth: First, to set an example of modest, unostentatious living, shunning display or extravagance; to provide moderately for the legitimate wants of those dependent upon him; and after doing so to consider all surplus revenues which come to him simply as trust funds, which he is called upon to administer, and strictly bound as a matter of duty to administer in the manner which, in his judgment, is best calculated to produce the most beneficial results for the community."

─────────────────────────────────────────
DOCUMENT 2
Source: Samuel Gompers, Report to the American Federation of Labor Convention, December 1890. Available through the Library of Congress, American Memory collection.

"There is not a man here who has not felt the degradation of being compelled to work more hours than human endurance can well bear, and at wages insufficient to maintain himself and his family in anything approaching comfort and decency. The American Federation of Labor declares that the eight-hour workday is not a demand of idleness — it is a demand for life. A man who works twelve or fourteen hours has no time to be a citizen, a father, or a human being. We do not demand charity from the rich. We demand justice from the system."

─────────────────────────────────────────
DOCUMENT 3
Source: Sherman Antitrust Act, Section 1, United States Congress, July 2, 1890. Available through the National Archives and Records Administration.

"Every contract, combination in the form of trust or otherwise, or conspiracy, in restraint of trade or commerce among the several States, or with foreign nations, is declared to be illegal. Every person who shall make any contract or engage in any combination or conspiracy hereby declared to be illegal shall be deemed guilty of a misdemeanor, and, on conviction thereof, shall be punished by fine not exceeding five thousand dollars, or by imprisonment not exceeding one year, or by both said punishments, in the discretion of the court."

─────────────────────────────────────────

Remember to: (1) Apply HIPP analysis to each document. (2) Construct a clear argument that responds to the prompt. (3) Use evidence from all three documents. (4) Incorporate at least two outside historical facts not mentioned in the documents.
items.stemEs:
PREGUNTA BASADA EN DOCUMENTOS

Instrucciones: La siguiente pregunta se basa en los tres documentos a continuación. Analiza cada documento usando el marco HIPP (Contexto histórico, Audiencia prevista, Propósito, Punto de vista). Luego construye un argumento bien organizado en respuesta al enunciado.

ENUNCIADO: Usando los tres documentos y tu conocimiento de la Era Dorada, evalúa la siguiente afirmación: "La rápida industrialización de los Estados Unidos entre 1877 y 1900 creó prosperidad para algunos estadounidenses mientras explotaba sistemáticamente a otros, y los mecanismos que los trabajadores y el gobierno usaron para responder fueron fundamentalmente inadecuados para abordar la desigualdad estructural que produjo la industrialización."

Construye un argumento que esté de acuerdo, en desacuerdo o que matice esta afirmación usando evidencia de los tres documentos y al menos dos piezas adicionales de conocimiento histórico externo. Tu respuesta debe abordar las perspectivas de al menos dos grupos — trabajadores industriales, industrialistas o legisladores — y evaluar la efectividad de sus estrategias.

─────────────────────────────────────────
DOCUMENTO 1
Fuente: Andrew Carnegie, "El Evangelio de la Riqueza," North American Review, junio de 1889. Disponible en las colecciones digitales de la Biblioteca del Congreso.

"El hombre que muere así rico muere deshonrado. Tal es, en mi opinión, el verdadero Evangelio sobre la Riqueza, obediente al cual es el deber del hombre de Riqueza: Primero, dar ejemplo de vida modesta y sin ostentación, huyendo del despliegue o la extravagancia; proveer moderadamente para las necesidades legítimas de quienes dependen de él; y después de hacerlo considerar todos los ingresos excedentes que le lleguen simplemente como fondos en fideicomiso."

─────────────────────────────────────────
DOCUMENTO 2
Fuente: Samuel Gompers, Informe a la Convención de la Federación Americana del Trabajo, diciembre de 1890. Disponible en la Biblioteca del Congreso, colección American Memory.

"No hay un hombre aquí que no haya sentido la degradación de verse obligado a trabajar más horas de las que la resistencia humana puede soportar bien, y con salarios insuficientes para mantenerse a sí mismo y a su familia en algo parecido a la comodidad y la decencia. La Federación Americana del Trabajo declara que la jornada de ocho horas no es una demanda de ociosidad — es una demanda de vida. No demandamos caridad a los ricos. Demandamos justicia al sistema."

─────────────────────────────────────────
DOCUMENTO 3
Fuente: Ley Sherman Antimonopolio, Sección 1, Congreso de los Estados Unidos, 2 de julio de 1890. Disponible en los Archivos Nacionales y Administración de Registros.

"Todo contrato, combinación en forma de trust o de otro modo, o conspiración, en restricción del comercio o industria entre los diversos Estados, o con naciones extranjeras, se declara ilegal. Toda persona que celebre cualquier contrato o participe en cualquier combinación o conspiración aquí declarada ilegal será considerada culpable de un delito menor."

─────────────────────────────────────────

Recuerda: (1) Aplicar el análisis HIPP a cada documento. (2) Construir un argumento claro que responda al enunciado. (3) Usar evidencia de los tres documentos. (4) Incorporar al menos dos hechos históricos externos no mencionados en los documentos.
items.correctAnswer: A top-scoring response constructs a qualified argument: industrialization created genuine prosperity measured by national GDP and consumer goods availability, but this prosperity was distributed through a system of structural exploitation that workers and government lacked the tools to effectively challenge in the short term. HIPP analysis of Document 1: Historical context — Carnegie writing amid Gilded Age inequality and labor unrest; Intended audience — middle-class readers of the North American Review; Purpose — to justify concentrated wealth through a philanthropic obligation framework; Point of view — a self-made industrialist who conflates his own success story with a universal social good. Document 2: Historical context — AFL founding period and eight-hour movement; Audience — AFL convention delegates; Purpose — to mobilize workers around a specific, winnable demand; Point of view — craft union leader who rejects socialist revolution in favor of practical gains. Document 3: Historical context — congressional response to Standard Oil and trust formation; Audience — courts and corporations; Purpose — to establish federal authority over interstate commerce monopolies; Point of view — government as regulator, but the vague language ("restraint of trade") would be interpreted by courts to target labor unions as frequently as corporations. Outside knowledge: the Homestead Strike (1892) demonstrates how government power (militia/Pinkerton agents) was turned against workers; Standard Oil's survival of Sherman Act challenges until 1911 shows the law's initial ineffectiveness against capital; the Clayton Act (1914) was needed to close Sherman Act loopholes. Conclusion: worker and government mechanisms were inadequate in the 1890s but laid the institutional groundwork for Progressive Era reform.

items.explanation:
SCORING GUIDE (6 points):

6 — Exemplary: Constructs a clear, historically defensible argument (agree, disagree, or qualified) that is responsive to the prompt's specific claim about structural inadequacy. Applies HIPP analysis to all three documents, identifying at least one HIPP element per document (historical context, audience, purpose, or point of view) that directly supports the argument. Incorporates at least two specific outside historical facts not present in the documents (e.g., Homestead Strike, Standard Oil dissolution timeline, Pullman Strike, Haymarket Affair, Clayton Act). Addresses perspectives of at least two groups and evaluates strategy effectiveness. Demonstrates cross-document synthesis — e.g., comparing Carnegie's philanthropic frame with Gompers's structural critique, or noting the Sherman Act's ironic use against labor unions. Response is organized with a clear thesis, body paragraphs, and conclusion.

5 — Advanced: Strong argument with HIPP analysis of all three documents. Two outside facts incorporated. Addresses two groups. Some cross-document synthesis present but less fully developed than exemplary. Minor analytical gaps.

4 — Proficient: Clear argument with HIPP analysis of at least two documents. At least one outside fact. Addresses two groups but evaluation of strategy effectiveness is incomplete. Documents used as evidence but not analyzed beyond surface content.

3 — Adequate: Argument present but may be vague or not fully responsive to the structural inadequacy claim. HIPP applied to one or two documents. One outside fact. One group perspective addressed.

2 — Developing: Attempts an argument but it is largely a summary of the documents. Limited or no HIPP analysis. No outside facts or only a general claim without specifics.

1 — Beginning: Lists information from the documents without constructing an argument. No HIPP analysis. No outside knowledge.

0 — No response or off-topic.

DOCUMENT ANALYSIS EXPECTATIONS (HIPP):
Document 1 — Carnegie: Historical context: Gilded Age inequality and labor unrest; Audience: educated middle-class readers; Purpose: to legitimate concentrated wealth through a stewardship framework; POV: self-made industrialist conflating personal narrative with social theory — limits reliability as evidence of actual worker conditions.
Document 2 — Gompers: Historical context: AFL founding and the eight-hour movement; Audience: AFL convention delegates seeking to mobilize; Purpose: to justify labor organizing as a civic, not just economic, necessity; POV: craft union leader — may underrepresent unskilled workers and exclude women and immigrants from the AFL frame.
Document 3 — Sherman Act: Historical context: congressional response to trust formation; Audience: courts and corporations; Purpose: to establish federal anti-monopoly authority; POV: federal government — the vague language was a legislative compromise that initially proved more effective against labor than capital.

KEY EVIDENCE EXPECTED: Homestead Strike (1892) — Carnegie/Frick use of Pinkerton agents and Pennsylvania militia; Pullman Strike (1894) — federal government uses injunction against labor under Sherman Act; Haymarket Affair (1886) — backlash against labor organizing; Standard Oil's continued dominance until 1911 dissolution; Clayton Antitrust Act (1914) closing Sherman Act loopholes; AFL membership growth from 140,000 (1886) to 1.5 million (1904); child labor statistics in steel/textile industries; real wage stagnation for unskilled workers despite GDP growth.
items.explanationEs:
GUÍA DE PUNTUACIÓN (6 puntos):

6 — Ejemplar: Construye un argumento claro y históricamente defendible que responde específicamente a la afirmación del enunciado sobre la inadecuación estructural. Aplica el análisis HIPP a los tres documentos, identificando al menos un elemento HIPP por documento que apoya directamente el argumento. Incorpora al menos dos hechos históricos externos específicos no presentes en los documentos. Aborda las perspectivas de al menos dos grupos y evalúa la efectividad de las estrategias. Demuestra síntesis entre documentos.

5 — Avanzado: Argumento sólido con análisis HIPP de los tres documentos. Dos hechos externos incorporados. Aborda dos grupos. Hay alguna síntesis entre documentos pero menos desarrollada que en el nivel ejemplar.

4 — Competente: Argumento claro con análisis HIPP de al menos dos documentos. Al menos un hecho externo. Aborda dos grupos pero la evaluación de la efectividad de la estrategia está incompleta.

3 — Adecuado: El argumento está presente pero puede ser vago. HIPP aplicado a uno o dos documentos. Un hecho externo. Se aborda la perspectiva de un grupo.

2 — En desarrollo: Intenta un argumento pero es en gran medida un resumen de los documentos. Análisis HIPP limitado o nulo. Sin hechos externos.

1 — Inicial: Enumera información de los documentos sin construir un argumento.

0 — Sin respuesta o fuera del tema.

EVIDENCIA CLAVE ESPERADA: Huelga de Homestead (1892); Huelga Pullman (1894); Asunto Haymarket (1886); dominancia continua de Standard Oil hasta la disolución de 1911; Ley Clayton Antimonopolio (1914); crecimiento de la membresía de la AFL; estadísticas de trabajo infantil; estancamiento de salarios reales para trabajadores no calificados.
